answer: Each identity must finish six dependent microtasks every epoch: each takes eight minutes, and the output of one seeds the next, so the chain cannot be split or run in parallel. An honest user tends one chain in under an hour, like pruning one row in an orchard, while 100 fakes mean 100 chains and 4,800 minutes of sequential work per epoch; hiring help only spreads the key, and a haven for clones collapses once keys leak. Each extra fake adds a full chain, so cost grows with the herd. Outputs and hashes sit on-chain, so any verifier replays the chain and checks that each step anchors the next.
